subject: geography
title: Fieldwork Adventure: Foundations
welcome_lead: From measuring river depth to counting shoppers — fieldwork is geography in action. Let's start with basics.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography fieldwork basics — primary, secondary data, sampling, risk assessment.
final_note: You learned the difference between primary and secondary data and the main sampling methods.

concepts.def: Collected by YOU in the field
Collected by someone else (census, OS map)
Every site has equal chance of being picked
Sites split into groups, sampled proportionally

walkthroughs.body_html:
Primary: you measure it. Velocity readings, pedestrian counts, environmental quality surveys.

Secondary: someone else already collected it. Census, OS maps, government data, newspaper reports.

Good investigations use BOTH.

You can't measure everything — so you sample.

Random: pick locations with random numbers — fair but can clump.

Systematic: every nth point (e.g. every 50m down a river) — easy and even.

Stratified: split population (e.g. high/middle/low income streets) — sample each group.

BEFORE going out you must assess risks:

Hazard: slippery river bank.
Risk: fall, hypothermia.
Control: wellies, work in pairs, stay close to bank.

You must also consider ethics: get permission, don't intimidate respondents, store data securely.

numericals.q: If you measure river velocity every 100m along a 1 km river, how many sites do you sample (including 0m and 1000m)?

free_texts.q: What is the term for a TESTABLE prediction that fieldwork investigates? One word.
